analysis.title: GS ETF Color - charts & bullets
key_insights: US-listed ETFs took in just over $200B in October, the second-largest month of flows in GS's dataset, bringing year-to-date flows to +$1.7T.
NDX fell 3.4% on the last trading day of October, a two standard deviation daily move, ending its worst month of the year. The broader market is still up double digits YTD.
ETFs that underperformed NDX in October saw larger inflows as a percentage of assets. Among that group, semis took the most inflows, followed by broad-based tech, EM and Brazil-exposed ETFs.
Levered ETFs had their largest month of inflows in GS's dataset (+$13B). On Friday alone they took in +$3B, the largest daily inflow YTD.
Levered ETF flows have historically been strongest on days of challenging price action (-2σ events) and weakest on the market's best days (+2σ).
NDX had its largest month of underperformance versus equal-weight SPX since 2002.
Health care returned +10% in October, its best month since April 2020. XLV took in +$1.6B, its best month of inflows since May 2022.
The desk faced supply for miners on Friday. COPX has fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, tying the longest weekly losing streak since the fund launched in 2010.
risk_factors: The report says the trading environment has grown increasingly complex after NDX's worst month of the year.
vol_and_positioning: NDX moved -3.4% on Friday, a two standard deviation daily move.
Levered ETF inflows reached +$13B in October and +$3B on Friday, both records or YTD highs in GS's dataset, and flows have historically been strongest on -2σ days.
The desk saw supply in miners on Friday, and COPX has declined 10 straight weeks.
